headline_marked: Court scuffle erupts as [[Jamaat leader Akhtaruzzaman denied bail]]
headline: Court scuffle erupts as Jamaat leader Akhtaruzzaman denied bail
summary: The retired major was sent to jail after a courtroom clash between BNP- and Jamaat-backed lawyers during his hearing.
details: Jamaat-e-Islami leader retired major Mohammad Akhtaruzzaman Ranjan has been sent to jail after his bail application was denied by a Dhaka court.
The proceedings were marked by chaos as a scuffle broke out between BNP- and Jamaat-backed lawyers in Metropolitan magistrate Jamshed Alam's court on Sunday.
The clash, triggered by a dispute over where lawyers could stand, forced the magistrate to temporarily leave the bench for his chamber.
Akhtaruzzaman was brought to court in handcuffs and wearing a helmet, facing charges of threatening the executive director of Shahjalal International Airport and assaulting a security supervisor.
The situation was eventually stabilized after interventions by state counsel Omar Faruq Faruqi and defence lawyer Abdur Razzaq, allowing the magistrate to return and conclude the hearing.
caption:
A courtroom clash between lawyers turns a bail hearing for Jamaat leader Akhtaruzzaman into chaos.

Jamaat-e-Islami leader retired major Mohammad Akhtaruzzaman Ranjan has been sent to jail after his bail application was denied by a Dhaka court.

The proceedings were marked by chaos as a scuffle broke out between BNP- and Jamaat-backed lawyers in Metropolitan magistrate Jamshed Alam's court on Sunday.

The clash, triggered by a dispute over where lawyers could stand, forced the magistrate to temporarily leave the bench for his chamber.

Akhtaruzzaman was brought to court in handcuffs and wearing a helmet, facing charges of threatening the executive director of Shahjalal International Airport and assaulting a security supervisor.

The situation was eventually stabilized after interventions by state counsel Omar Faruq Faruqi and defence lawyer Abdur Razzaq, allowing the magistrate to return and conclude the hearing.

Source: Prothom Alo, bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune

headline_marked: 2,089 hospitalised as [[6 more die of dengue]] in 24 hours
headline: 2,089 hospitalised as 6 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: Total dengue deaths in Bangladesh have risen to 262, with over 5,800 patients currently undergoing treatment across the country.
details: According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), at least six dengue patients died and 2,089 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00 am today.
Of the six deaths, three were reported in the Khulna division, two in Dhaka South City Corporation, and one in the Mymensingh division.
The latest figures bring the total number of dengue deaths in the country to 262, while the total number of cases has reached 86,458.
Currently, 5,849 dengue patients are receiving treatment at various hospitals across Bangladesh.
caption:
6 deaths and 2,089 hospitalisations in just 24 hours. Dengue continues to surge across Bangladesh.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), at least six dengue patients died and 2,089 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00 am today.

Of the six deaths, three were reported in the Khulna division, two in Dhaka South City Corporation, and one in the Mymensingh division.

The latest figures bring the total number of dengue deaths in the country to 262, while the total number of cases has reached 86,458.

Currently, 5,849 dengue patients are receiving treatment at various hospitals across Bangladesh.
